title: A joint N-body fit of TESS transit times (2019-2024) and 545 RVs gives HD 191939 c a mass of 6.3 +- 0.6 Earth masses and reduces the reported 4-sigma TTV-RV tension to 2.4 sigma
abstract: A prior campaign result found anticorrelated transit timing variations (TTVs) of HD 191939 c and d and a TTV mass of c of 2.4 +- 0.8 Earth masses, about 4 sigma below the radial-velocity (RV) mass of 8.0 +- 1.0. We measured 111 TESS transit times of b, c and d again (2-min and 20-s data, sectors 15-86), calibrated the timing errors with 450 injected transits (error scale 1.01-1.15), and fitted the times and 545 public RVs (CARMENES, HARPS-N, HIRES, APF) with a six-planet TTVFast N-body model in which the outer planets are also free. Our times agree with the prior times (RMS 1.0-1.8 min), so the change comes from the model. The joint fit gives m_c = 6.3 +- 0.6 and m_d = 4.1 Earth masses with aligned eccentric orbits (e_c = 0.10, e_d = 0.08) and fits the TTVs to chi2 = 12.8 (23 times) and 13.4 (16 times). Profile likelihoods give m_c = 5.6 +0.7/-0.8 from the transit times alone and 8.3 +- 0.9 from the RVs alone, a 2.4-sigma difference; separate TTV and RV masses for b, c and d improve 2 Delta lnL by 8.7 for 3 parameters (p = 0.03). The transit times alone exclude m_c = 2 (Delta chi2 = 50). Both the d TTVs and the RVs reject the published 101.12-d period of planet e (Delta lnL = 43); the fit gives 101.84 d. The masses do not change with a Rayleigh eccentricity prior, without four flagged transits, or with planet e inclined by 10 degrees. The b-c-d-e-f solution is regular for 10,000 years (MEGNO 2.0); the fitted orbit of the candidate g is chaotic. TESS sectors 117-131 (about 2027-2028) can test m_c = 8: that solution differs from the best one by up to 6 min (c) and 18 min (d). Limitations: profile likelihoods from a local optimiser instead of a full posterior, coplanar orbits, no RV activity model, and only TESS photometry.

display.caption: Profile Delta chi2 of the mass of HD 191939 c from the TESS transit times (red), the RVs (blue) and both together (black). Shaded bands: the published RV mass (8.0 +- 1.0) and the prior campaign TTV mass (2.4 +- 0.8).

O-C diagrams of HD 191939 b, c and d (TESS 2019-2024, this work) with the best joint TTV+RV N-body fit (red, m_c = 6.3) and the best fit with m_c fixed at the RV value 8.0 (blue), extended through the approximate span of TESS sectors 117-131 (yellow).
All 38 timed 2-min TESS transits of HD 191939 c (red model) and d (blue model), detrended, with O-C and calibrated errors in the panel titles.

citations.reason: We re-measure and refit the HD 191939 c and d TTVs that this work detected. Our times agree with its times, but our joint TTV+RV fit with free outer planets gives m_c = 6.3 +- 0.6 and excludes its m_c = 2.4. We used its table for the starting period of d and for a comparison figure.
